description.narrative:
After years of protracted crisis, Sudan plunged into a conflict of alarming scale in mid-April 2023 when fighting between the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group, broke out initially in the capital Khartoum, and quickly expanded to other areas across the country.
Conflicts hotspots are in Khartoum and El Gezira and West and South Darfur. A high number of displacements are from Khartoum and North Darfur. Of the 18 states in Sudan, there is fighting in 11. So only 7 are safe at the moment. Because White Nile is close the South Sudan border many IDPs are flowing there so they can cross the border easily and quickly if needed.
There are currently over 10m internally displaced people and over 2.1 million people have crossed borders since the outbreak of the conflict. Between 2000 and 4000 people are crossing the border daily into South Sudan. Large numbers have crossed into Chad, Egypt and it is unclear how many have moved through South Sudan and to Uganda but it is believed to be many. There are not many formal camps so people are setting up in schools, market places and open areas where it is safe. Food insecurity is worst in areas which are conflict hotspots. HAC has over 400 informal sites where IDPs are settling in White Nile State. Needs there include shelter, food, health support, protection and nutrition interventions. NGOs are present but facing challenges because of the sheer scale of displacement and need. The food security situation is expected to deteriorate around the lean season in August and September. Continued blockades restrict access to those bringing aid. Rains are expected now and flooding in expected in White and Blue Nile states. Many displaced people are still living out in the open so needs will increase. Commodity prices are increasing
CAFOD launched an appeal to support the humanitarian response from supporters in the UK and this programme has been designed to deliver this support.
